speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Will, and I'm here to talk to you about automated code review.
zh: 我叫 Will,今天我要和大家谈谈自动化代码评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: My teammate, Amaya, and I work at Uber, and we're going to be walking through uReview, a system that Uber has built to help increase the velocity of our software engineering teams.
zh: 我和我的队友 Amaya 在 Uber 工作,我们将带大家了解 uReview,这是 Uber 构建的一个系统,用来帮助我们软件工程团队提升速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a little bit of context about what software engineering org at Uber looks like, we have thousands of software engineers who work across hundreds of teams located across 12 different sites, and they work in primarily one of six language-specific monorepos.
zh: 先简单介绍一下 Uber 软件工程组织的概况:我们有数千名软件工程师,分布在数百个团队,遍布 12 个不同的办公地点,他们主要工作在六个按语言划分的单体仓库之一中。

speaker: Unknown
en: As many of you have probably noticed over the past 24 months, the volume of PRs, the size of PRs has been growing.
zh: 正如你们许多人在过去 24 个月中可能注意到的那样,PR 的数量和 PR 的大小一直在增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the ways that that's been exposed to us has been through the metric that we track of the first time to review.
zh: 暴露这个问题的方式之一,就是我们追踪的一项指标:首次评审时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back in 2024, we were seeing that engineers would get their first review within three hours.
zh: 回到 2024 年,我们看到工程师能在三小时内获得首次评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, in 2026, that has grown to nine hours, in addition to all of the volume changes.
zh: 而到了 2026 年,在所有这些数量变化之外,这个时间已经增长到了九个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in short, code review is now the bottleneck that we are running into.
zh: 简而言之,代码评审现在成了我们遭遇的瓶颈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically around automated code review, there are various options available in the industry, but Uber spent the time to invest in building an in-house solution due to some of the constraints that we have.
zh: 具体到自动化代码评审,行业里有各种可选方案,但由于我们自身的一些约束条件,Uber 花时间投入构建了一个内部解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of those is we currently use Fabricator and have for a long time and are in the process of migrating to GitHub.
zh: 其中一个约束是,我们目前使用 Fabricator 并且已经用了很长时间,目前正处于向 GitHub 迁移的过程中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of the solutions do not provide support for Fabricator.
zh: 大多数解决方案都不提供对 Fabricator 的支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: In addition, if you were at the previous talk, you saw Uday and Adam talking about the agentic SDLC.
zh: 此外,如果你听了上一场演讲,你会看到 Uday 和 Adam 谈到了智能体化的 SDLC。

speaker: Unknown
en: A big part of what we want to do is bring a consistent code review experience to the inner loop so that our agents are getting the same code review, the same rules, everything applied, as our humans do.
zh: 我们想做的一件重要事情,就是把一致的代码评审体验带入内循环,让我们的智能体获得与人类相同的代码评审、相同的规则、同样的全部流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: With hundreds of teams across the company, we can't have centralized management of our code reviews, our customizations, our rules, and even the knowledge that goes into those code reviews.
zh: 公司有数百个团队,我们无法对代码评审、自定义配置、规则,乃至代码评审所涉及的知识进行集中管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to distribute that.
zh: 我们需要把这一切分散出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a need for plugging into an existing team ownership system rather than trying to replicate that externally.
zh: 所以我们需要接入现有的团队所有权系统,而不是试图在外部复制一套。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, with the volume of code reviews that we perform, we need the ability to take factors like the risk profile and the complexity of a code change and factor that in when deciding how we're going to run a code review.
zh: 最后,鉴于我们所执行的代码评审的数量,我们需要能够把风险画像、代码变更的复杂度等因素纳入考量,以此决定如何运行代码评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all code gets the exact same review.
zh: 并非所有代码都会得到完全相同的评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, consistency.
zh: 最后还有一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to make sure that we have security and compliance reviews run across everything.
zh: 我们需要确保安全和合规评审在所有代码上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can't rely on teams
zh: 我们不能依赖各个团队

speaker: Unknown
en: Hoping to run the skill, the code review skill that happens.
zh: 去指望运行那个技能、那个会发生的代码评审技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need reliability there.
zh: 我们需要在这方面有可靠性。

speaker: Unknown
en: With all that said, I wanted to give you an overview of the architecture of what uReview looks like.
zh: 说了这些,我想给大家概述一下 uReview 的架构是什么样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk about a couple of the big pieces, and then we're going to dive into a few focus areas.
zh: 我们会先讲几个大的部分,然后深入几个重点领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the top, you'll notice that we have our code review surface areas, GitHub, Fabricator, and the agent loop.
zh: 在最上面,你会看到我们有代码评审的入口面,GitHub、Fabricator 以及智能体循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: These all feed into UReview service.
zh: 这些都汇入 UReview 服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: This takes in requests for reviews.
zh: 它接收评审请求。

speaker: Unknown
en: It brings in feedback from users.
zh: 它收集用户的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it routes it.
zh: 并对请求进行路由。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a number of different generators.
zh: 我们有许多不同的生成器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, these generators are tuned for different performance and cost avenues.
zh: 这些生成器针对不同的性能和成本路径做了调优。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have the ability to plug into third-party code review systems so that we can compare ourselves to what's available more broadly.
zh: 我们还有能力接入第三方的代码评审系统,这样我们可以把自己和市面上更广泛的方案做比较。

speaker: Unknown
en: Finally, with all these different generators, we might be duplicating comments, and we can actually create quite a high volume of comments.
zh: 最后,有这么多不同的生成器,可能会产生重复的评论,而且实际上会产生数量相当大的评论。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've ever used AI to run a code review, you've probably seen that.
zh: 如果你曾经用 AI 运行过代码评审,你可能见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we run through a number of steps in the post-processing where we both rate, categorize, filter, and deduplicate comments so that our engineers get only the highest confidence comments that are actionable for them to work on.
zh: 所以我们在后处理中经过若干步骤,对评论进行评分、分类、过滤和去重,让我们的工程师只拿到置信度最高、可操作的评论去处理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll also notice along the bottom, we talk a little bit about feedback in our evaluation.
zh: 你还会注意到,在底部,我们会稍微谈谈反馈和我们的评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: But with this context of the overall system, I'm now going to hand it off to Amaya to dive into our first focus area.
zh: 有了对整个系统的这个背景了解,我现在要把话筒交给 Amaya,让她深入讲我们的第一个重点领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello.
zh: 你好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hello, everyone.
zh: 大家好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I will be talking about how we evolve view review with observability and evaluation.
zh: 我要讲的是我们如何通过可观测性和评估来演进 view review。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Ureview had a very humble beginning.
zh: Ureview 一开始非常简陋。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically, it was a single prompt that you should do logic checks per file, a simple agent which used to do thorough review.
zh: 基本上,它就是一个单一的提示词,让你对每个文件做逻辑检查,再配一个做彻底评审的简单智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had a dispatcher to decide which generator to choose.
zh: 我们还有一个调度器来决定选择哪个生成器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even what we used to collect as observability was very surface level.
zh: 甚至我们当时收集的可观测性数据也非常表面化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to collect cost.
zh: 我们收集成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: We used to run an NPS survey, have Google Forms being filled, Slack support.
zh: 我们会做 NPS 问卷调查,让人填 Google 表单,还有 Slack 支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with all of this, we saw that our quality to cost ratio was like all over the place.
zh: 凭着这一切,我们发现我们的质量成本比简直一团糟。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like our goal is to be in the second quadrant, that is the top left quadrant, but
zh: 我们的目标是处于第二个象限，也就是左上角的那个象限，但是

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see we were all over the place.
zh: 你可以看到，我们当时各处都有分布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then what we did is that we started collecting more data.
zh: 接下来我们做的是开始收集更多数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started collecting the sentiments of the replies that were made to the UReview, that the UReview
zh: 所以我们开始收集针对 UReview 所做回复的情绪倾向，也就是 UReview

speaker: Unknown
en: YouReview agent got from the developers.
zh: 这个智能体从开发者那里得到的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we categorized them into positive, negative.
zh: 我们把它们分为正面、负面。

speaker: Unknown
en: We classified them into various categories, and we found a bunch, a lot of classes of bugs and issues that we could actually solve.
zh: 我们把它们归类到各种类别中，然后我们发现了一大堆、非常多种类的 bug 和问题，而这些是我们实际上可以解决的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that, we improved the system, and we were able to move a large number of PRs to a high quality to cost ratio.
zh: 借助这些，我们改进了系统，并且能够把大量的 PR 移到高质量成本比的区间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we still felt that this was not enough.
zh: 但我们仍然觉得这还不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to know more of how the review is done.
zh: 我们需要更多了解评审是如何完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started tracking things like addressal rate.
zh: 所以我们开始追踪诸如处理率（addressal rate）这样的指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So basically, when a UReview comment is made, does the developer go and actually address the comment?
zh: 基本上，就是当一条 UReview 评论被发出时，开发者是否真的去处理了这条评论？

speaker: Unknown
en: We started tracking that.
zh: 我们开始追踪这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also started doing more like a runtime profile, which is like the agent trajectory, which told us
zh: 然后我们还开始做更多类似运行时画像（runtime profile）的东西，也就是智能体的轨迹（trajectory），它告诉我们

speaker: Unknown
en: Why the agent is doing what it did.
zh: 智能体为什么做了它所做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get to know what tool calls it made.
zh: 我们能知道它做了哪些工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: We get to know what thinking process it had.
zh: 我们能知道它经历了怎样的思考过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then with that insight, we were able to actually tune our runtime, tune our performance, such that the agent could very quickly give us high quality results at a low cost.
zh: 有了这些洞察，我们就能够真正调优我们的运行时、调优我们的性能，让智能体能够以低成本非常快速地给我们高质量的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the biggest learnings in this process was the model doesn't know that it's wrong.
zh: 在这个过程中最大的一个体会是，模型不知道自己是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It always confidently says 100% sure that, yeah, this is the review for your code, go ahead.
zh: 它总是充满自信地说 100% 确定，没错，这就是对你代码的评审，放手去做吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we saw that, no, it actually needs a lot of guidance from the teams because each team has its own style guide, its own patterns or anti-patterns that they want to look for.
zh: 但我们看到，不，它实际上需要来自团队的大量指导，因为每个团队都有自己的风格指南、自己想检查的模式或反模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that all should be baked into the agent.
zh: 所以这些都应该内置到智能体里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also realize that we need to have guardrails for the agent.
zh: 我们也意识到，我们需要为智能体设置护栏。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we need to tell the agent what not to waste turns doing.
zh: 所以我们需要告诉智能体不要把轮次浪费在哪些事情上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like code review is something that has to happen in like a specific time span.
zh: 比如，代码评审是必须在特定时间跨度内完成的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if it starts spending time doing things that it should not be doing, leads to a bad quality code review.
zh: 而如果它开始把时间花在不该做的事情上，就会导致质量很差的代码评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: Second focus area for you review has been .
zh: YouReview 的第二个重点领域是。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went very deep on team customizations because as Will presented that we have hundreds of teams and everyone has like their own way or their own thing for code review.
zh: 我们在团队定制化方面走得很深，因为正如 Will 所讲的，我们有数百个团队，每个团队在代码评审上都有自己的一套方式、自己的那一套东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our review stack is pretty straightforward.
zh: 所以我们的评审栈是相当直截了当的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have single file reviewers and multi-file reviewers.
zh: 我们有单文件评审器和多文件评审器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We basically do a general purpose, hey, find me all logic bugs per file kind of a review.
zh: 我们基本上做的是一种通用型的、「嘿，帮我找出每个文件里所有的逻辑 bug」这样的评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also do a deep review because we have like six monorepos.
zh: 然后我们还做深度评审，因为我们有大约六个 monorepo。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all these monorepos have their own anti-pattern style guides and all baked into this agent review, which does a nice multi-file review.
zh: 所有这些 monorepo 都有各自的反模式、风格指南等等，都内置到了这个智能体评审中，它会做很好的多文件评审。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then we extended it further basically to AI linters.
zh: 但接着我们把它进一步扩展，基本上到了 AI linter。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are basically few-shot AI prompt or like a few-shot system where developers can basically kind of deterministically get more context and then run rules with that context and like a file and find some systematic and mechanical issues.
zh: 这些基本上是少样本（few-shot）AI 提示，或者说是一个少样本系统，开发者基本上可以确定性地获取更多上下文，然后带着这些上下文对一个文件运行规则，从而找出一些系统性的、机械性的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, the most powerful thing is the custom agent, where the teams could basically define their own custom agent, link it to a knowledge base, link it to their past PRs, have a skill to do the review, and so on.
zh: 最后，最强大的东西是自定义智能体，团队基本上可以定义他们自己的自定义智能体，把它链接到一个知识库，链接到他们过去的 PR，赋予它做评审的技能，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But all of this was not simple because we had to actually piggyback on our ownership model, which is at Uber, so that we can very logically roll out to all the teams.
zh: 但所有这些都不简单，因为我们必须实际上搭上我们在 Uber 的所有权模型（ownership model）的便车，这样我们才能非常合理地推广到所有团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to basically do a, what do you say, co-locate the customizations next to where the developers write their code so that they can quickly keep updating these customizations.
zh: 我们基本上要做——怎么说呢——把定制化放置在开发者编写代码的地方旁边，这样他们就可以快速持续地更新这些定制化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to implement a smart deterministic routing so that we could route which team gets what kind of review with which model, what kind of generators, and so on.
zh: 我们必须实现一个智能的确定性路由，这样我们就能路由哪个团队得到哪种评审、用哪个模型、哪种生成器，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, the hard thing was like we had to actually surface all of this observability that I talked before.
zh: 最后，困难的地方在于，我们必须真正把我之前谈到的所有这些可观测性都呈现出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the agent trajectory, address rate, sentiment analysis back to the teams so that the teams could actually understand that, oh, I wrote this rule, but maybe not a lot of developers are liking it in my team, so let me go and update it.
zh: 比如智能体轨迹、处理率、情绪分析，反馈给各个团队，这样团队才能真正理解：哦，我写了这条规则，但也许我们团队里没有很多开发者喜欢它，那让我去更新它吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we had to give bubble up that kind of observability to all the people who are contributing to the platform.
zh: 然后我们还必须把这类可观测性向上冒泡，提供给所有为这个平台做贡献的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that we learned is that actually writing the skill was very easy.
zh: 我们学到的一点是，实际上编写技能（skill）非常容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like teams just very quickly wrote a skill by asking Claude to write one, go over my previous PR reviews and write me a skill.
zh: 团队只要让 Claude 写一个技能就很快写出来了：「去翻遍我过去的 PR 评审，给我写一个技能」。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the hard part was how to run these skills at scale with consistent quality and low cost.
zh: 但困难的部分是如何以一致的质量和低成本大规模运行这些技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that required a lot of iterations, not only from the Euroview team side, but also like for each team who was trying to write these rules.
zh: 而这需要大量的迭代，不仅来自 YouReview 团队这一侧，也来自每个试图编写这些规则的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: In results, we basically see that UReview does around 25,000 comments a week, and we get 10% of them actually get some feedback, and only 4% of the PRs actually get some negative feedback.
zh: 在结果方面，我们基本上看到 UReview 每周发出大约 25,000 条评论，其中 10% 真正得到了一些反馈，而只有 4% 的 PR 真正收到了负面反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also saw that
zh: 我们还看到，

speaker: Unknown
en: The overall addressal rate was around 67%.
zh: 整体处理率大约是 67%。

speaker: Unknown
en: And almost three quarters of the high severity issues were usually addressed by the developers, which shows that Euroview actually adds some value to the entire development lifecycle.
zh: 而将近四分之三的高严重性问题通常都会被开发者处理，这表明 YouReview 实际上为整个开发生命周期增加了一些价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then with all the observability and evals that I went through, we saw that against like a very naive implementation, our costs were down by 60% and our quality and our accuracy was up by around 70%.
zh: 然后,通过我经历的所有可观测性和评估,我们发现,和一个非常朴素的实现相比,我们的成本下降了 60%,我们的质量和准确率提升了大约 70%。

speaker: Unknown
en: For our last focus area, I'll give the mic back to Will and he will go over the inner versus outer loop.
zh: 对于我们最后一个重点领域,我会把话筒交回给 Will,他将讲解内环与外环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now that we've talked about some of the details of actually implementing high-quality reviews, it kind of brings us to the last area, which is where we start talking about where things are going, right?
zh: 那么,既然我们已经谈了实际实现高质量代码评审的一些细节,这就把我们带到了最后一个领域,也就是我们开始谈论事情正走向何方,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: With moving to the agentic SDLC, we're moving software into a model where engineers are interacting with the code less.
zh: 随着转向智能体化 SDLC,我们正在把软件推向一种工程师与代码交互更少的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're oftentimes not as involved in authoring the code.
zh: 他们通常不再那么深度参与编写代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Currently, we still have humans approving the code, but we see a short path in the near future to a percentage of our code landing automatically, having automatic approvals.
zh: 目前,我们仍然由人类来批准代码,但我们看到在不久的将来有一条很近的路径,让一部分代码自动合入、获得自动批准。

speaker: Unknown
en: Various parts of the industry are already moving there.
zh: 业界的各个部分已经在朝那里走了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Part of the way along the process was figuring out by having our single code review platform, what did we need to tune for the various audiences that are actually getting these code reviews?
zh: 这个过程的一部分,是通过拥有我们这个单一的代码评审平台,弄清楚我们需要为实际接收这些代码评审的各类受众调优什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the interface, that's one area that's sort of intuitive there.
zh: 你知道,界面,这是其中一个比较直观的方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing that might be less intuitive is around accuracy.
zh: 一件可能不那么直观的事情是准确率。

speaker: Unknown
en: With the inner loop, our accuracy needs actually need to go up.
zh: 在内环中,我们实际上需要让准确率进一步提高。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or else we can result in dealing with cavitation of an agent where it fixes something, goes back, gets another code review, and has to kind of like fix backwards because the quality of the comment was low.
zh: 否则我们可能会陷入智能体的空转:它修复了某个问题,回头又收到一次代码评审,然后不得不反向再修一遍,因为那条评论的质量很低。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the other interesting things is agents are more than happy to go through and fix 100 nits on a pull request where your engineers really get frustrated in situations like that.
zh: 另一件有趣的事情是,智能体非常乐意去把一个拉取请求里的 100 个小瑕疵全部修掉,而这种情况会让你的工程师非常沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: But probably the most interesting aspect of this transition is the feedback.
zh: 但这次转型中最有意思的方面大概是反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you can see, quite a bit of what went into getting high-quality code reviews at Uber was bringing the human feedback into the system and using that to figure out how to tune our prompts, how to tune our agents.
zh: 如你所见,在 Uber 获得高质量代码评审的过程中,相当大一部分是把人类反馈引入系统,并利用它来弄清楚如何调优我们的提示词、如何调优我们的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as we move to a model where humans are less in the loop, where software engineering is moving to an agentic model,
zh: 因此,随着我们转向人类更少介入的模式、软件工程转向智能体化模式,

speaker: Unknown
en: We're effectively going to a place where we're starting to talk about, are we going to kill the outer loop?
zh: 我们实际上是走向一个我们开始谈论的地方:我们要不要杀死外环?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is the human engineer not going to be involved in the code review?
zh: 人类工程师会不会不再参与代码评审?

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are already here.
zh: 有些人已经到了这一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, with the feedback taken into consideration, you start wondering, all right, what could this result in, right?
zh: 现在,把反馈考虑进去之后,你会开始琢磨:好吧,这可能导致什么结果,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll let your imagination go there in terms of quality degradation, slop, and so forth.
zh: 我就让你们的想象力去发挥吧,比如质量退化、垃圾内容等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: But rather than killing the outer loop,
zh: 但与其杀死外环,

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that we believe and the industry has just started to really kind of coalesce on this idea that we're really expanding the outer loop.
zh: 我认为——我们相信,而且业界也刚刚开始真正凝聚到这个想法上——我们实际上是在扩展外环。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather than removing humans from the code review process, we are moving their responsibilities up a layer.
zh: 与其把人类从代码评审流程中移除,我们是把他们的职责上移一层。 [[124? no]]

speaker: Unknown
en: Rather than them dealing with the details of the implementation, the agent is great at writing the software.
zh: 与其让他们处理实现细节,智能体很擅长写软件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent is getting much, much better at reviewing the software as a human would.
zh: 智能体在像人类一样评审软件方面也正变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But now, as software engineers, we still are going to have an outer loop.
zh: 但现在,作为软件工程师,我们仍然会有一个外环。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just going to look a little different.
zh: 只是它会看起来有点不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of you worrying about the optimization of the performance and the API compatibility, you're going to be thinking more about architecture in your code reviews.
zh: 你不再是去担心性能优化和 API 兼容性,而是在代码评审中更多地去思考架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to have time to focus on the domain expertise that you have.
zh: 你会有时间去专注于你所拥有的领域专长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And product thinking.
zh: 还有产品思维。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we believe that as we adopt this automated code review, this is going to be the result of how our engineers are interacting with the system and guiding it.
zh: 所以我们相信,随着我们采用这种自动化代码评审,这将是我们工程师与系统交互并引导它的方式的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's it.
zh: 就是这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for coming.
zh: 非常感谢大家的到来。
